# CONFIGS.md — the CONFIGURATION-SURFACE TABLE (Phase A / gate for Phase B)

Mechanically derived from the C source: every meaningful **combination** of
(runtime option / mode / flag) × (input shape) that the C code actually treats
differently for *valid* input. Rows come from the `if` / `switch` / `#ifdef`
branches the C takes, the block / rate / chunk boundaries its loops distinguish,
and the FULL set of public entry points — including the lowest-level ones, not
just the one-shot convenience wrappers.

Build configuration: **no `HAVE_*` macros**, **no `NDEBUG`** (portable/ref/soft
implementations, live `assert()`). Target x86-64 Linux.

Each row is exercised with **many randomised inputs** (fixed seed) by the named
test, comparing the C `.so` and the Rust `.so` byte-for-byte through `dlsym`.

## Build-time configuration surface (feature combinations)

`Cargo.toml` declares **no `[features]` table at all**, and `grep -rn 'cfg(feature'
src/ tests/` finds **0 matches**. The power set of declared features therefore has
exactly **one** element — the empty set — so `--no-default-features` and the plain
default build are the same single configuration:

| # | cargo invocation | features | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `cargo check/test --no-default-features` | (none) | OK |
| 1' | `cargo check/test` (default) | (none) | OK — identical to #1 |

Enumerated and verified automatically by `.phaseA/feature_matrix.sh`, which reads
the feature names out of `Cargo.toml`, builds their power set, and runs
`cargo check` / `cargo test` for each element (so it stays correct if features are
ever added):

```sh
$ .phaseA/feature_matrix.sh check
=== Build-time configuration surface ===
Cargo [features] declared : 0 (none)
default feature set       : (none)
cfg(feature = ...) in src : 0 files

=== 1 feature combination(s) to verify ===
OK: <no features>
OK: default
```

The only `#[cfg]` gates in `src/` are architecture gates
(`target_arch = "x86_64" | "aarch64" | "x86" | "arm"` and the portable
`not(any(...))` fallback) plus one `cfg(test)`. They are selected by the target
triple, not by a Cargo feature, so they do not multiply the combination count on
a fixed target (x86-64 Linux here).

The **C** side has an analogous single configuration: `c_src/CMakeLists.txt`
defines **no `HAVE_*` macros** and passes no `-DNDEBUG`
(`C_DEFINES = -Dsodium_EXPORTS`, `C_FLAGS = -fPIC -std=gnu99`), so every
`#ifdef HAVE_*` takes the portable branch (`ref` / `ref10` / `soft` / `nosse` /
`donna32` / `fe_25_5`) and `assert()` is live. The Rust crate reproduces exactly
that configuration, which is why one Cargo configuration suffices.
